checks.result: J_ij=∂_j U_i and W a=Ω×a/2 have consistent curl signs. Independent index contraction tests pass.
Direct differentiation of tau and y gives the stated positive collapse and stretching signs; manufactured time-dependent test passes.
Y=y+(C/c_l)e_z removes C; translations of the field U_h(y)=U(y-h e_z) correspond to C_h=C-c_l h. Coordinate-translation wording should specify this convention.
Independent tensor calculation gives div Rm=δ+V·∇δ+tr(J²)+ΔP. The nonzero divergence correction is essential.
Independent manufactured compressible test verifies curl Rm=Rω+δΩ.
Expanding Ω×V=(J-Jᵀ)V and ∇|V|²/2 reproduces Rm, including the C-dependent center.
Dot the vorticity equation with Ω and use ∇|Ω|²=0. Requires a nonzero interior extremum; not a normalization.
Independent symbolic and numerical rescaling tests verify U_a=aU(y/a), P_a=a²P(y/a), C_a=aC. Vorticity amplitude is invariant.
Angular basis differentiation produces both geometric terms. Independent physical-coordinate and cylindrical finite differences agree on off-axis tests.
Proper rotation Q preserves the equations and C e_z; simultaneous transverse parity is the required symmetry.
Cylindrical modes are even; horizontal Cartesian components shift by ±1. Quadratic terms generate higher even frequencies.

The revised zero-mode Parseval factor and full spectral classification are correct: axisymmetry requires all nonzero cylindrical modes to vanish; four-fold symmetry requires every occupied frequency to be divisible by four. E2 alone does not classify fundamental period.
For O e_z=±e_z, Q commutes with O; transform C with the corresponding sign. Velocity is polar and vorticity is axial under reflections.
The explicit seed formula transforms correctly under orthogonal matrices commuting with M, including inversion and z-reflection. These are branch restrictions unless released.

For smooth fields, parity gives odd horizontal and even vertical transverse degrees. The displayed O(r^3) remainder uses third-order regularity, not merely C2. Divergence gives a+d+wprime=0; n=2 horizontal velocity may be O(r).
For smooth Cartesian fields, a scalar angular mode has r^|k| times a smooth function of r². The ±1 component shift gives the stated coupled orders.
Finite smooth representations do not prove derivative convergence of a limiting profile. The listed checks are required numerical evidence, not a theorem of convergence.
S²=S by Q²=I.
The revised determinant factor and axial-vector reflection law are correct. The proper Q rotation commutes with curl and enforces exact divergence freedom.
The product divergence term must be kept; potential envelopes avoid it. Chain rules are with respect to physical coordinates.

The bounded representation permits angular tails and added fractional degrees, but no completeness theorem is established. Its generic degree d-2 velocity correction must cancel for Euler balance below one half; adding the second envelope does not itself enforce cancellation. See research/bounded-tail-expansion/PROOF.md.
No free amplitude of Ω is provided. Canonical translation alone is not a profile symmetry; C allows a coordinate recentering.

A resolved global max gives the stated scale gauge. A fixed-grid or fixed-weight surrogate requires local sensitivity and interior-resolution checks. The proposed pressure-n=2 phase gauge degenerates when that coefficient vanishes, as it does for the initial seed. No P(0) loss was found in the current numerics loss, consistent with its P∞=0 architecture.

D^k U_a=a^(1-k)D^k U(y/a); global first-derivative norms are scale invariant and second derivatives can fix scale. Values at the origin are invariant, while a fixed nonzero point moves in the unscaled profile. Rotation phase may be fixed by a suitable nonzero tensor component.

checks.section: 7.1 exact affine family, scalar factor clause
checks.result: Cayley-Hamilton gives the complete Q-equivariant homogeneous linear family as stated. The no-scaling assertion for the vortical family requires nonzero skew M; symmetric matrices in its overlap remain affine solutions after scaling. General affine solutions also allow an axial constant plus linear pressure.

The constant-velocity/linear-pressure field is correctly identified as unforced and excluded by decay. The separate spectral parentheticals in this same section remain incorrect; see the dedicated row below.
The required distinctions are mathematically appropriate. Check completion separately; no diagnostic list proves the properties automatically.
The homogeneous multiplier vanishes at d=1-1/c_l, giving all stated exponent ranges. This is an assumed matching class, not an exhaustive theorem.
Spherical divergence gives div_S A_T+(d+2)A_r=0; integrate over S² and use d+2≠0.
At degree 2d-1 the multiplier is -1. The formal cascade is a possible hierarchy; an arbitrary exact tail expansion is not proved to contain only those powers.

Integrating f=partial_i partial_j(U_i U_j) gives mass boundary O(R^(2d+1)) and dipole boundary O(R^(2d+2)); hence zero monopole for d<-1/2 and zero dipole for d<-1, under derivative-compatible decay. Higher moment divergence and additional matched multipole degrees are correctly qualified.

The core exponent is 5c_l-2. For a nonzero angular leading tail the fixed-ball power of tau cancels, local L² requires d>-3/2, and the profile itself need not lie in L² at infinity. Strong matching is an additional hypothesis.

The all-p interval hypothesis agrees with the two independently saved primary arXiv texts. This check does not independently establish the journal version. Bounded derivatives or adequate cutoff assumptions must accompany the quoted vorticity argument.

With regularity and natural derivative decay, the integrals and signs are justified in research/whole-space-integrals/PROOF.md. Finite-radius quadrature with no analytic tail bound remains a numerical consistency check.

Primary v3 checked. Keep finite-energy plus gradient-growth hypotheses for 2.1; p>max(3c_l,1) for 3.4; nonzero Ω and local outgoing at a zero for 3.8; decay, normalization and finite nodal set in Definition 3.7 for 3.9; axisymmetry and (3.5),(3.8) for 4.5.
v1.1 removes the unsupported quantitative conclusion and asks for a resolved nonzero n=2 signal.
At a zero with Ω≠0, JΩ=SΩ=Ω; trace then gives the stated incoming direction and eigenvalue sum. It is conditional and must not be imposed when Ω=0.
Same statement as 1.3(d). A numerically refined local extremum is not a global maximum certificate.

The revised localized cylindrical formulas follow by substitution in the independently derived curl. The n=2 criterion, k=-0.04 and transverse transport determinant -0.2075 at cl=.45 check directly. Homogeneous at infinity means an asymptotic leading term.
Correctly labeled initializer in the lead file. Direct tests find momentum, vorticity and pressure defects. Its R^(d-2) correction generally fails nonlinear tail balance below one half.
The termwise L² denominator is well defined away from degeneracy. Use physical weights for physical norms. Quantiles/maxima stay sampled quantities. Proposed numeric thresholds are screening choices.
The viscosity coefficient is nu exp[-(1-2c_l)s]. Decay of that coefficient alone establishes no NS singularity.

32 independent calibrations and nine independent synthetic decoder cases pass. A copied trainer suite has 15 passing tests and the pilot500 matched holdout agrees to 3e-13 relative. These do not certify every later source revision or the unresolved lifecycle repairs.

The revised text correctly excludes a nonzero smooth divergence-free, curl-free natural homogeneous leading tail. Independent componentwise spherical harmonic proof is research/irrotational-leading-tail/PROOF.md. The previous audit used obsolete allowance wording against a v1.2 snapshot; that attribution is corrected here.

E2=E4=0 is not sufficient for axisymmetry (a nonzero n=6 field is a counterexample). E2=0 is not sufficient for four-fold symmetry (n=4 and n=6 together have period pi). Replace these clauses by the corrected section 3.3 criteria.

A nonzero d_3 U alone does not exclude a two-dimensional field invariant in another direction. Use the smallest eigenvalue of the integrated derivative Gram matrix over all directions, as the independent evaluator does.

With Omega in Lp, bounded strain K in operator norm, and vanishing cutoff boundary terms, integration yields (1-3cl/p) integral|Omega|^p = integral(Xi.S.Xi)|Omega|^p. For p<3cl/(1+K), the coefficient is less than -K, forcing zero. Regularize at Omega=0 for p<2.

The primary v3 meridional fixed-point swirl equation is (1-2cl)Utheta=0. Nonzero swirl forces cl=1/2; this point is not a zero of the full three-dimensional transport. The revised distinction is correct.

Rotational periodic wedge identification, release of temporary anti-axisymmetry penalties, the symmetric-part test for a quadratic outgoing inequality, third derivatives of A for vorticity, and limits of finite root finding are appropriate. Completion is checked separately.

A negative real eigenvalue is not always present. For U=(-x/2-a*y,a*x-y/2,z), a nonzero, spec(DV)={c-1/2+ia,c-1/2-ia,c+1}. Use negative-real-part eigenvalue. Rank two does give two nonzero real eigenvalues of opposite signs; rank three need not.

At rank two the implicit function theorem contains the full nearby zero set in a C2 arc; it can initially be a closed subset of that arc. Only the subsequent connected-alpha argument supplies an actual equilibrium subarc. Say isolated point or closed subset of a C2 arc.

Nonzero constant U=b with P=-(1-c)b dot y is an exact sublinear solution. The theorem gives no nonconstant sublinear profile, or no nonzero profile under global decay. Use those words instead of no nontrivial profile without defining nontrivial.
Sublinear unbounded growth is included. Replace growing velocity in the exclusion list by failure of sublinearity, including affine backgrounds.

The qualitative compactness floor concerns true whole-space absolute L-infinity momentum residual under all fixed class bounds. A relative residual requires a specified uniformly bounded denominator and global norm before this implication follows. Finite-sample relative training or holdout residual is insufficient. Merely decreasing toward a positive floor is also possible.

The theorem statement Omega=0 and U constant under C2, uniform U=o(R), 0<c<1/2 is independently proved. Its decaying specialization excludes the full primary class. See THEORY_V3_AUDIT.md and research/uncountable-stagnation/PROOF.md.
